title: Gut Microbiome Metabolism Links High Fat Diets to Immunotherapy Efficacy.
screening_reason: Focuses directly on gut microbiome metabolism and its linkage to high fat diets and immunotherapy efficacy.
summary_ja: 本論文は高脂質食と免疫療法の有効性をつなぐ腸内細菌叢代謝の役割に関する研究報告である。論文抄録の本文データは提供されていないが、タイトルから高脂質食が腸内細菌代謝を介してがん免疫療法の奏効性に及ぼす影響に焦点を当てていることが示されている。腸内細菌叢が生成する代謝産物が免疫応答を調整するメカニズムの解明が期待される。
summary_en: This paper focuses on how gut microbiome metabolism links high-fat diets to the efficacy of immunotherapy. Although abstract text is omitted, the title highlights the interaction between dietary lipid content, microbial metabolic pathways, and cancer immunotherapy outcomes.
key_finding_ja: 高脂質食が腸内細菌代謝を介して免疫療法の効果に影響を与える可能性が提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事因子と腸内細菌代謝ががん免疫療法の治療奏効性に与える影響を解明する手がかりとなる可能性がある。

title: Gut dysbiosis impairs HPA axis function and exacerbates post-stroke inflammation in high-fat diet-fed male mice.
abstract: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced metabolic stress is associated with impaired hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis function, but its impact on stroke outcomes and the role of the gut microbiota remain unclear. In a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model, we found that HFD induced gut dysbiosis, suppressed hypothalamic CRH expression, and reduced circulating corticosterone, which in turn exacerbated neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, and worsened neurological recovery. Interventions with fecal microbiota transplantation or supplementation of Akkermansia muciniphila partially restored HPA axis activity, mitigated inflammatory injury, and improved behavioral outcomes post-stroke. These findings suggest that a gut microbiota-HPA axis may be relevant under metabolic stress conditions and open a possible microbiota-based adjunctive strategy for improving stroke prognosis in metabolically vulnerable populations. Importance Metabolic disorders such as obesity and high-fat diet exposure are known to worsen stroke outcomes, but the mechanisms connecting metabolic stress, gut microbiota alterations, and neuroendocrine dysfunction have not been well defined. Our data indicate that gut dysbiosis under HFD conditions is associated with HPA axis suppression and worse neuroinflammatory injury after stroke and that microbiota-targeted intervention can restore hormonal regulation and functional recovery. This highlights the gut microbiota-neuroendocrine interface as a promising area for therapeutic exploration in metabolically at-risk stroke patients.
authors: Zhong H, Jin Z, Liu Y, Wang Y, Liu Y.
screening_reason: Examines how high-fat diet-induced gut dysbiosis impairs HPA axis function, exacerbates post-stroke neuroinflammation, and can be rescued by Akkermansia muciniphila supplementation.
summary_ja: 高脂質食による代謝ストレス下では腸内細菌叢の乱れが生じ、脳卒中後の神経炎症が増悪することが報告されています。マウスの脳梗塞モデルにおいて、高脂質食は視床下部のCRH発現および血中コルチコステロン濃度を抑制し、脳内の炎症と神経細胞死を悪化させました。糞便微生物移植やAkkermansia muciniphilaの補充を行うことで、HPA軸の活性が一部回復し、神経炎症と行動障害が改善しました。本研究は、代謝異常下における腸内細菌叢-HPA軸の関連性と、その制御による予後改善の可能性を示しています。
summary_en: High-fat diet-induced gut dysbiosis was found to suppress HPA axis activity and worsen neuroinflammation and functional recovery after stroke in male mice. Interventions such as fecal microbiota transplantation or Akkermansia muciniphila supplementation partially restored HPA axis function, reduced neuroinflammatory injury, and improved behavioral outcomes. These findings indicate that targeting the gut microbiota-neuroendocrine axis may offer a potential therapeutic strategy for stroke under metabolic stress.
key_finding_ja: 高脂質食による腸内細菌叢の乱れはHPA軸の機能を抑制し、脳卒中後の神経炎症や行動障害を悪化させることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 代謝リスクを有する脳卒中患者において、腸内細菌叢を標的とした介入が神経内分泌系の調節や予後改善の新たなアプローチとなる可能性が期待される。

title: From gut to brain: data-driven evidence suggests causal contribution of gut-microbiota to major depressive disorder in humans.
abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a highly prevalent, severe mental health condition that constitutes one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. While recent animal studies suggest a causal role of the gut microbiome in the pathophysiology of MDD models, evidence in humans is still unclear due to small sample sizes, inconsistent clinical assessment of MDD diagnosis, and methodological limitations regarding causal inference in cross-sectional data. Here, we explicitly address these shortcomings to investigate the potential causal link between the gut microbiome and MDD: First, we replicate previously reported microbiome-depression associations using one of the largest multicenter MDD cohorts for which microbiome data and in-depth diagnostic assessment are available (N = 1,269 MDD patients and controls). We find a significant difference between healthy controls and MDD patients for the relative abundance of four taxa: Eggerthella , Hungatella , Coprobacillus , and Lachnospiraceae FCS020. Second, we employ state-of-the-art, fully data-driven causal inference tools within Judea Pearl's framework, allowing us to derive model constraints from the data rather than relying on potentially strong, unrealistic assumptions. Using this approach, we found evidence for Eggerthella and Hungatella as potential causal contributors to MDD. Furthermore, we show that the potential causal effects of Eggerthella and Hungatella on MDD persist beyond the influence of body mass index, revealing two distinct potential causal pathways linking the gut microbiome to MDD. Finally, the difference in relative abundance of these taxa between healthy and MDD patients was independent of antidepressant medication. Our study provides the first data-driven evidence for a potential causal role of gut microbiota in the pathophysiology of depression in humans.
authors: Fehse L, Ribeiro AH, Winter NR, Thanarajah SE, Fisch L, Welzel M, Bang C, Meinert S, Flinkenflügel K, Borgers T, Goltermann J, Leehr EJ, Bloemendaal M, Natasha EE, Mulder D, Arias Vasquez A, Stein F, Thomas-Odenthal F, Usemann P, Teutenberg L, Nenadic I, Straube B, Alexander N, Jamalabadi H, Jansen A, Nitsch R, Lügering A, Reif A, Kittel-Schneider S, Cryan J, Franke A, Valderrama B, Clarke G, Lavelle A, Dannlowski U, Kircher T, Heider D, Hahn T.
screening_reason: Evaluates the potential causal contribution of human gut microbiota composition to the pathophysiology of major depressive disorder.
summary_ja: 大うつ病性障害（MDD）患者と対照群の計1,269名を対象とした多施設コホートにおいて、腸内細菌叢とMDDの関連性を解析しました。解析の結果、Eggerthella、Hungatellaを含む4つの菌株の相対存在量に有意な差が見られました。データ駆動型の因果推論手法を用いることで、EggerthellaとHungatellaがMDDに対する潜在的な因果寄与因子であることが示唆されました。この効果はBMIや抗うつ薬の使用とは独立して認められました。
summary_en: Using a multicenter cohort of 1,269 individuals, this study analyzed the potential causal link between the gut microbiome and major depressive disorder. Four bacterial taxa differed significantly in abundance between MDD patients and controls, with data-driven causal inference identifying Eggerthella and Hungatella as candidate causal contributors. These potential causal associations persisted independently of body mass index and antidepressant medication usage.
key_finding_ja: ヒトコホートのデータ駆動型因果推論解析により、EggerthellaおよびHungatellaが大うつ病性障害の発症に潜在的に因果寄与している可能性が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: ヒトにおける特定腸内細菌とうつ病との因果関係の可能性が示されたことで、微生物を標的とした新たな診断・治療介入の開発につながる期待があります。

title: Carabrone alleviates neuroinflammation by covalently targeting ubiquitin conjugating enzyme UBE2D3 in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an incurable and progressive inflammatory disease of the central nervous system (CNS) characterized by inflammatory demyelination, chronic axonal damage, and neurodegeneration. Carabrone (CA), a sesquiterpene lactone from the traditional Chinese herb Carpesium abrotanoides L., demonstrates diverse pharmacological properties. However, its therapeutic effects on MS and the underlying mechanisms remain unexplored. In the present study, we reported the beneficial effects of CA on experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a well-established mouse model of MS, for the first time. Treatment with CA markedly attenuated disease progression induced by myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG 35-55 ) peptide, as evidenced by reduced clinical severity, diminished inflammatory cell infiltration into the CNS, and a decrease in demyelinated lesions. Mechanistically, CA could covalently bind to the cysteine 85 (Cys85) residue of ubiquitin conjugating enzyme E2 D3 (UBE2D3), thereby inhibiting the phosphorylation of inhibitor of nuclear factor-kappa B alpha (IκBα) and its subsequent ubiquitin-mediated degradation, ultimately leading to suppression of the nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway. These findings were further confirmed in macrophages via siRNA-mediated knockdown of UBE2D3. Taken together, our results revealed that CA is a novel UBE2D3 inhibitor and provided a promising therapeutic candidate for MS.
authors: Tang H, Sun L, Jia B, Xu T, Xiao J, Zhang R, Wang T, Ji SL, Xu Y.
screening_reason: The study demonstrates that carabrone mitigates neuroinflammation in EAE by covalently binding and inhibiting the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme UBE2D3.
summary_ja: 本研究では、多発性硬化症（MS）のマウスモデルである実験的自己免疫性脳脊髄炎（EAE）に対する生薬由来成分カラブロン（CA）の治療効果と機序を調査した。CAの投与はEAEマウスの臨床的重症度を軽減し、中枢神経系への炎症細胞浸潤および脱髄病変を抑制した。分子メカニズムとして、CAはユビキチン結合酵素UBE2D3のCys85残基に共有結合し、IκBαの分解とNF-κBシグナル伝達の活性化を阻害することが示された。
summary_en: This study demonstrated the therapeutic potential of carabrone (CA), a sesquiterpene lactone, in an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mouse model of multiple sclerosis. CA administration significantly reduced clinical severity, CNS inflammatory infiltration, and demyelination in EAE mice. Mechanistically, CA covalently bound to the Cys85 residue of UBE2D3, suppressing IκBα degradation and NF-κB pathway activation.
key_finding_ja: カラブロンはUBE2D3に共有結合してNF-κB経路を抑制することにより、EAEマウスにおける神経炎症と病態進行を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 動物モデルでの知見でありヒトへの有効性検証は今後の課題だが、多発性硬化症に対する新しい標的分子や治療薬候補の提案につながる。

title: Age-Associated Differences and Rearing Strategy-Related Alterations in the Gut Microbiome of Captive African Elephants (Loxodonta africana).
abstract: The gut microbiome is critical for the health and dietary adaptation of African elephants (Loxodonta africana), but how age and rearing strategies influence microbial communities remains unclear. Understanding these factors is essential for improving conservation and captive management practices, particularly given the high mortality rates in formula-fed calves. Using 16S rRNA sequencing and clinical data from 17 African elephants (calves: breastfed n = 3, formula-fed n = 2; adults n = 12), we investigated age-associated differences in gut microbiome composition and explored the potential relationship with rearing practices. Due to the limited sample size, results from formula-fed calves were analyzed as exploratory. Healthy adults were dominated by Bacteroidota, a phylum linked to fiber digestion, and showed higher microbial diversity compared to breastfed calves. Exploratory analysis of formula-fed calves revealed distinct compositional features, including reduced Bacteroidota and Lachnospiraceae and enrichment of Gammaproteobacteria, which co-occurred with clinical signs of diarrhea, growth failure. This study highlights age-associated differences in the gut microbiome of healthy African elephants and suggests that formula-feeding may be associated with altered microbial composition. These findings provide a foundation for future research to optimize rearing protocols for captive elephant calves.
authors: Duan Y, Li J, Li Z, Wang Z, Zhang M, Bi Z.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates age- and rearing strategy-associated differences in the gut microbiome of African elephants.
summary_ja: 本研究では、飼育下のアフリカゾウ17頭を対象に、腸内細菌叢の加齢による変化と人工乳育ちの幼獣における影響を16S rRNAシーケンス解析により調べた。健康な成獣では食物繊維消化に関与するBacteroidota門が優勢であり、母乳育ちの幼獣よりも微生物多様性が高かった。探索的な解析において、人工乳で育った幼獣ではBacteroidota門などの減少とGammaproteobacteria綱の増加が認められ、下痢などの臨床症状と並行していた。
summary_en: This study evaluated age-associated and rearing-related changes in the gut microbiome of 17 captive African elephants using 16S rRNA sequencing. Healthy adults demonstrated higher microbial diversity dominated by Bacteroidota compared with breastfed calves. Exploratory findings suggested that formula-fed calves exhibited altered gut microbiota, including reduced Bacteroidota and increased Gammaproteobacteria, alongside clinical signs like diarrhea.
key_finding_ja: 飼育下のアフリカゾウにおいて、成獣と幼獣で腸内細菌叢の構造が異なり、人工乳飼育の幼獣では特定の細菌群の偏りと消化器症状が観察された。
why_it_matters_ja: サンプル数が限定された探索的観察であるためさらなる検証が必要だが、絶滅危惧種の人工飼育プロトコル改善に向けた基礎情報となり得る。

title: Semaglutide Alleviates LPS-Induced Cognitive Disorder via O-GlcNAcylation of AKT-mTOR Signaling Pathway Components.
abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) manifests as neurocognitive alterations induced by anesthesia and surgical stress. High-risk factors, including advanced age, obesity, diabetes, and preoperative neurological dysfunction, accelerate PND progression, with neuroinflammation serving as a core pathological mechanism throughout PND pathogenesis. Semaglutide regulates neuroinflammation in patients with diabetes and stroke, yet its role in PND remains undefined.A lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory neurocognitive impairment mouse model was established via intracerebroventricular injection. Mice were treated with semaglutide alone or combined with the O-GlcNAc transferase inhibitor OSMI-1 and AKT-silencing adeno-associated viruses. Behavioral, biochemical and immunofluorescence assays were performed to evaluate cognitive function and molecular changes. Semaglutide significantly rescued LPS-induced cognitive deficits and restored hippocampal O-GlcNAcylation. Mechanistically, LPS inhibited AKT O-GlcNAc modification and AKT-mTOR pathway activity, facilitated mTOR-gephyrin binding, disrupted GABAAR distribution, aggravated neuronal apoptosis, and impaired synaptic plasticity. Semaglutide reversed these abnormalities by elevating AKT O-GlcNAcylation to activate the AKT-mTOR pathway, which triggered mTOR-gephyrin dissociation, restored synaptic GABAAR localization, attenuated neuronal damage, and rescued synaptic plasticity.Semaglutide ameliorates PND via AKT O-GlcNAcylation-mediated AKT-mTOR activation and subsequent neuroprotective effects.
authors: Liu Q, Chen L, Zhang M, Wang Z, Wang X, Dong Y, Wang K, Jiang C, Yin Y.
screening_reason: Examines covalent post-translational protein modification (O-GlcNAcylation) in alleviating neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits.
summary_ja: LPS投与により誘発された周術期神経認知障害（PND）モデルマウスにおいて、セマグ ルチドの神経保護効果とその詳細な分子メカニズムが検討されました。LPS処理はAKTのO-GlcNAc修飾およびAKT-mTOR経路を抑制し、認知機能障害と神経アポトーシスを引き起こしました。セマグ ルチドの投与は、AKTのO-GlcNAc修飾を高めることでAKT-mTOR経路を再活性化し、GABAARのシナプス局在を回復させて認知機能を改善しました。本研究は、PNDにおけるセマグ ルチドの治療効果にタンパク質の翻訳後修飾が関与していることを示しています。
summary_en: Semaglutide was found to attenuate LPS-induced cognitive deficits in a mouse model of neurocognitive disorder. Mechanistically, semaglutide enhanced O-GlcNAcylation of AKT, which reactivated the AKT-mTOR pathway, triggering mTOR-gephyrin dissociation and restoring synaptic GABAAR distribution. These findings demonstrate that semaglutide exerts neuroprotective effects through AKT O-GlcNAcylation-mediated signaling.
key_finding_ja: セマグ ルチドはAKTのO-GlcNAc修飾を増加させてAKT-mTOR経路を活性化し、LPS誘発性の認知機能障害を改善することが解明された。
why_it_matters_ja: 周術期神経認知障害（PND）に対するセマグ ルチドの新たな分子機序が明らかになったことで、翻訳後修飾を標的とした治療戦略の創出につながる可能性がある。

title: HABP4/VIM-Mediated Focal Adhesion Assembly Regulates Enteric Neural Crest Cell Migration via the FAK/SRC Pathway.
abstract: Background The enteric nervous system (ENS) arises from enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs), and defects in this process can lead to Hirschsprung's disease (HSCR), a congenital disorder characterized by the absence of enteric neurons in the distal colon. Our previous work has identified HABP4 as a potential susceptibility gene for HSCR; however, the mechanisms by which it regulates ENS development remain unclear. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with immunofluorescence staining was used to characterize the spatiotemporal expression pattern of HABP4 in mouse intestinal tissues. HABP4-knockdown human embryonic stem cell-derived neural crest cells (hESC-derived NCCs) were generated to evaluate its role in ENS development, and cell migration was assessed using Transwell assays. Protein-protein interaction network analysis integrated with transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify HABP4-interacting partners and downstream signaling pathways, which were further validated by AlphaFold-based structural modeling and co-immunoprecipitation. In addition, pharmacological rescue experiments were conducted to examine the functional involvement of key downstream effectors, and the pathogenicity of HABP4 variants identified in HSCR patients was further evaluated. Results HABP4 was highly and specifically expressed in ENCCs. Knockdown of HABP4 significantly impaired the migratory capacity of hESC-derived NCCs. Transcriptomic analysis revealed significant enrichment of focal adhesion-related gene sets following HABP4 knockdown. Mechanistically, HABP4 interacted with VIM to promote focal adhesion assembly and activate the FAK/SRC signaling cascade, thereby facilitating ENCCs migration. Notably, treatment with a focal adhesion kinase (FAK) agonist partially rescued the migration defects induced by HABP4 knockdown, and the HABP4 variant (R379W) identified in HSCR patients was found to impair ENCCs migration. Conclusion HABP4 is localized at the leading edge of migrating ENCCs, where it interacts with VIM to promote focal adhesion assembly and activate FAK/SRC signaling.
authors: Lin H, Xiao J, Zheng Z, Zhou J, Li R, Shen Z, Li H, Feng J, Chen F.
screening_reason: Investigates the molecular mechanisms regulating enteric neural crest cell migration during enteric nervous system development.
summary_ja: ヒルシュスプルング病（HSCR）の病態解明に向け、腸管神経前駆細胞におけるHABP4の役割が調べられました。単一細胞RNAシーケンシングなどの解析により、HABP4は腸管神経節前駆細胞（ENCC）に特異的に高発現し、ノックダウンにより細胞遊走能が著しく低下することが確認されました。メカニズムとして、HABP4はビメンチン（VIM）と相互作用して焦点接着の形成を促し、FAK/SRCシグナル経路を活性化させることが判明しました。さらに、HSCR患者で特定されたHABP4変異体（R379W）もENCCの遊走能を低下させることが示されました。
summary_en: This study demonstrated that HABP4 is highly expressed in enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs) and is required for their migratory capacity during enteric nervous system development. Mechanistically, HABP4 interacts with VIM to promote focal adhesion assembly and activate FAK/SRC signaling. Furthermore, a human HABP4 variant identified in Hirschsprung's disease patients was shown to impair ENCC migration.
key_finding_ja: HABP4はビメンチンとの相互作用を通じて焦点接着の形成とFAK/SRCシグナルを活性化し、腸管神経節前駆細胞の遊走を制御していることが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: HABP4による腸管神経前駆細胞遊走の分子機構の解明は、ヒルシュスプルング病の発生要因の理解および診断・治療法の開発に貢献する可能性がある。

title: Microbial metabolite-driven mechanisms linking the gut microbiome to atherosclerosis: multi-omic and translational perspectives.
abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and a substantial residual risk persists despite optimal management of traditional risk factors. Increasing evidence implicates the gut microbiome as a mechanistic contributor to atherogenesis, not merely through taxonomic shifts but via the production of bioactive microbial metabolites that link diet, microbial metabolism, and host vascular biology. These metabolites have emerged as central effectors of the gut-artery axis, influencing intestinal barrier integrity, systemic immunity, lipid handling, and thrombosis. Among the best-characterized pathways, trimethylamine N -oxide and phenylacetylglutamine have been robustly linked to macrophage lipid accumulation, platelet hyperreactivity, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. More recently, imidazole propionate, a histidine-derived microbial metabolite, has emerged as a candidate mediator of vascular inflammation and plaque development through imidazoline-1 receptor-dependent activation of mTORC1 signaling, supported by mechanistic and experimental evidence. Advances in metagenomics, metabolomics, and proteomics now enable systems-level interrogation of microbiome-host interactions, facilitating causal inference through integrative metabolite-protein and pathway-level analyses. These approaches have revealed reproducible molecular networks associated with subclinical and clinical atherosclerosis, providing a framework for biomarker discovery and therapeutic targeting. People with HIV represent a particularly informative human model, in which persistent gut barrier disruption and dysbiosis sustain immune activation and confer excess cardiovascular risk, with distinct microbial and metabolite signatures linked to vascular inflammation and plaque progression. This review synthesizes current evidence linking gut microbial function to atherosclerosis, with a specific focus on metabolite-driven mechanisms, multi-omic integration, and translational relevance. We highlight emerging biomarkers and therapeutic strategies targeting microbial metabolic pathways and discuss methodological challenges that must be addressed to advance the gut-artery axis toward precision cardiovascular medicine.
authors: Masiá M, Gutiérrez F.
screening_reason: Focuses on bioactive microbial metabolites linking gut microbiome function and host metabolic pathways to vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、腸内細菌叢由来の生理活性代謝物が動脈硬化症の病態に与える影響について解説しています。トリメチルアミン-N-オキシド（TMAO）やフェニルアセチルグルタミンに加え、イミダゾールプロピオン酸などの代謝物が血管炎症やプラーク形成に関与することが示されています。マルチオミクス解析の進展により、腸内細菌と宿主の相互作用ネットワークの解明が進み、精密医療への応用が期待されています。特にHIV感染者モデルなどにおける持続的な腸管バリア破綻と血管炎症との関連についても議論されています。
summary_en: This review summarizes current evidence linking gut microbial function and derived metabolites, such as TMAO, PAG, and imidazole propionate, to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis. Advances in multi-omics integration allow systems-level interrogation of gut-artery interactions to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Addressing methodological challenges will be essential to translate these microbial metabolic pathways into precision cardiovascular medicine.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌代謝物が腸管バリア機能、血管炎症、脂質代謝などを介して動脈硬化の発症や進行を制御するメカニズムが総括された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌由来の代謝経路を標的とした介入法やバイオマーカーの確立により、心血管疾患の個別化医療に向けた新たな展開が期待される。

title: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits.
abstract: Gut bacteria affect host physiology, but the underlying mechanisms are not completely understood. We identify a pathway whereby gut microbes convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into mobile bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that are distributed systemically and affect host metabolism. Electron paramagnetic resonance detected DNICs in tissues of conventional but not germ-free mice. Mouse and human feces and E. coli generated DNICs from nitrate and iron citrate, whereas a nitrate-reductase-deficient mutant did not. Dietary supplementation with nitrate+iron citrate or synthetic DNICs increased tissue DNIC levels and ameliorated cardiometabolic dysfunction in Western diet-fed mice. Additionally, in HepG2 cells and human hepatocyte spheroids, DNIC reduced fatty acid-induced steatosis. DNIC bioactivity is mediated by the Fe(NO) 2 entity, rather than by free nitric oxide (NO), and involves activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC), inhibition of leucine uptake, and mTORC1 signaling normalization. Modulating DNIC formation by the gut microbiota could be a strategy to support cardiometabolic health.
authors: Kleschyov AL, Shimari M, Boeder AM, Schiffer TA, van Riet S, Pironti G, Bork NI, Rotmann A, Zhuge Z, Guimarães DD, Picozzi G, Moretti CH, Carvalho LRRA, Nihlén C, Closs EI, Nikolaev VO, Ingelman-Sundberg M, Weitzberg E, Lundberg JO, Carlström M.
screening_reason: Identifies a novel microbial metabolic pathway where gut bacteria convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into systemic bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes that regulate host metabolism.
summary_ja: 腸内細菌が無機硝酸塩と非ヘム鉄からジニトロシル鉄錯体（DNIC）を生成し、宿主の代謝に影響を与える経路が特定されました。通常マウスの組織ではDNICが検出されましたが、無菌マウスでは検出されず、硝酸還元酵素欠損株の大腸菌もDNICを生成しませんでした。西洋食を与えたマウスへの硝酸塩とクエン酸鉄の補給または合成DNICの投与は、組織のDNICレベルを高め、心血管代謝障害を改善しました。DNICは可溶性グアニル酸シクラーゼの活性化などを通じて脂肪化を抑制することが示されました。
summary_en: Gut microbes convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that are systemically distributed and modulate host metabolism. Dietary supplementation with nitrate and iron citrate or synthetic DNICs elevated tissue DNIC levels and improved cardiometabolic dysfunction in Western diet-fed mice. The bioactivity of DNICs involves activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase, inhibition of leucine uptake, and normalization of mTORC1 signaling.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌が生成するジニトロシル鉄錯体（DNIC）が宿主の代謝を修飾し、高脂質食負荷に伴う心血管代謝障害を改善することが解明された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌によるDNIC生成経路の制御が、心血管代謝の健康を維持・改善するための新たな治療戦略につながる可能性がある。

title: Fermentation capacity of the gut microbiota influences exercise motivation and neuroendocrine integration.
abstract: Physical inactivity contributes substantially to global disease burden, yet the physiological mechanisms underlying exercise motivation remain poorly understood. The gut-brain axis presents a potentially modifiable target for behavioral intervention. Emerging evidence demonstrates that the gut microbiota influences motivated behaviors, but the specific metabolic functions and physiological mechanisms mediating these effects remain poorly defined. Here, we demonstrate that the predicted fermentation capacity of the gut microbiota influences voluntary wheel running (VWR) acquisition and neuroendocrine integration during exercise in C57BL/6J mice. Antibiotic-induced microbiome depletion reduced VWR acquisition, while shifting predicted function toward aerobic respiration and away from anaerobic fermentation. Supplementation with short-chain fatty acids, the primary fermentative products, restored normal VWR activity in microbiome-depleted mice. Conversely, 4-week dietary pretreatment with 2.5% prebiotic fiber (inulin) increased predicted fermentative capacity of the microbiota and VWR activity above baseline levels. Microbiome manipulation produced bidirectional dysregulation of corticosterone responses to exercise: acute antibiotic depletion increased post-exercise concentrations, while germ-free development decreased them, despite elevated striatal catecholamines. This exercise-specific uncoupling reveals microbiome-dependent integration of metabolic demand signals in the coordination of sympathetic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis responses. Furthermore, the inulin-induced enhancement in VWR activity was associated with increased striatal histamine concentrations following exercise, suggesting additional mechanisms of neuromodulation. These findings demonstrate that the fermentative capacity of the gut microbiota influences exercise motivation and neuroendocrine regulation, providing novel insights into dietary interventions targeting physical activity. Importance Physical inactivity is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, and our lack of understanding of the biological forces driving motivation to exercise limits our ability to develop interventions that enhance engagement. Using a rodent model of voluntary exercise along with microbiota depletion and metabolite replacement, we uncovered that the gut microbiota and its capacity to ferment dietary components into short-chain fatty acids drive exercise habit acquisition and help facilitate coordination between neurochemical signals and systemic stress hormones during exercise. Additionally, microbiome depletion "uncoupled" these systems, resulting in dysregulated stress responses during forced exercise. Finally, we showed that enhancement of microbiota fermentation capacity via dietary addition of prebiotic fiber was able to increase exercise engagement while also enhancing concentrations of histamine, a neuromodulator that potentiates locomotor activity, in the striatum. These findings suggest that the gut microbiome is a modifiable target for behavior change that facilitates integration of metabolic demand in neuroendocrine activity. Collectively, this work provides a mechanistic foundation to support the use of dietary interventions in sedentary populations to start exercise habits.
authors: Hutchinson NT, Maino-Vieytes CA, Valls C, Allen J, Rund LA, Johnson RW, Woods JA.
screening_reason: Investigates how the fermentative metabolic capacity of the gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids regulate exercise motivation and neuroendocrine integration via the gut-brain axis.
summary_ja: マウスモデルにおいて、腸内細菌叢の予測発酵能が自発的運動習慣の獲得と運動時の神経内分泌統合に影響を与えることを示しました。抗菌薬による腸内細菌の枯渇は自発運動量を減少させましたが、短鎖脂肪酸の補充により運動量が回復しました。プレバイオティクス食物繊維の投与は細菌叢の発酵能を高め、運動量を増強させました。また、細菌叢の操作は運動負荷時のコルチコステロン応答と脳内モノアミン系との統合に変化をもたらすことが観察されました。
summary_en: In mice, the predicted fermentation capacity of the gut microbiota significantly influenced voluntary wheel running and neuroendocrine integration during exercise. Antibiotic depletion reduced voluntary running, which was restored by short-chain fatty acid supplementation, while prebiotic fiber enhanced running performance above baseline. Microbial manipulation also uncoupled stress hormone responses from central neurochemical signals during exercise.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢の発酵能および短鎖脂肪酸産生が、自発的運動意欲と運動時における神経内分泌・ストレス応答の調節に関与している。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事による腸内細菌叢の発酵能向上が、運動習慣の獲得や運動時のストレス応答最適化に役立つ可能性を示しています。

title: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii attenuates diabetes-associated affective disorders by suppressing neuroinflammation through the SCFAs/FFAR3/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway.
abstract: Background Diabetes-associated affective disorders are a global health burden tightly linked to the gut microbiota. The depletion of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii (F. prausnitzii) is a shared feature of diabetes and depression, yet its therapeutic potential and mechanisms remain unclear. Methods We first analyzed the microbial composition of populations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and major depressive disorder (MDD) using the GMrepo database to potential probiotic candidates. We then investigated whether supplementation with this probiotic could ameliorate anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in a T2DM mouse model. Utilizing integrated multi-omics analysis, we assessed alterations in gut microbiota profiles and fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) levels, combined with molecular biology experiments to evaluate the impact on neuroinflammation, intestinal barrier integrity, HPA axis activity, and monoamine neurotransmitter levels. Finally, the molecular mechanisms underlying this anti-neuroinflammatory effect were further explored. Results We identified a marked depletion of F. prausnitzii in individuals with T2DM and in those with MDD. Administration of F. prausnitzii to T2DM mice ameliorated anxiety and depression-like behaviors, reversed gut dysbiosis, and elevated butyric and valeric acids levels. These improvements were coupled with enhanced intestinal barrier integrity, normalized HPA axis activity, and restored monoamine neurotransmitter levels. Moreover, the anti-neuroinflammatory effects elicited by F. prausnitzii-derived butyric acids and valeric acids appeared to be associated with the FFAR3/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway. Conclusions Our findings suggest that SCFA-induced FFAR3 pathway may contribute to the anxiolytic- and antidepressant-like effects of F. prausnitzii, highlighting its potential as a microbiome-based strategy for managing diabetes-associated affective disorders.
authors: Zhang Y, Mo D, Huang Q, Mou X, Dai Q, Zhao W, Li N, Lin X.
screening_reason: Demonstrates how gut bacteria (Faecalibacterium prausnitzii) and their SCFA metabolites attenuate neuroinflammation and affective behavioral deficits.
summary_ja: 2型糖尿病（T2DM）および大うつ病性障害（MDD）のデータ解析により、Faecalibacterium prausnitziiの減少が示されました。T2DMマウスモデルに本菌を投与したところ、不安・うつ様行動が軽減し、腸内細菌叢の乱れや短鎖脂肪酸レベルが回復しました。さらに、腸管バリア機能の向上、HPA軸の正常化、モノアミン神経伝達物質の回復が認められました。F. prausnitzii由来の酪酸およびバレル酸による抗神経炎症効果は、FFAR3/NF-κB/NLRP3経路と関連していることが明らかにされました。
summary_en: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii depletion was identified as a common feature in type 2 diabetes and major depressive disorder. Administration of F. prausnitzii in a diabetic mouse model reduced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, restored short-chain fatty acid levels, and reinforced intestinal barrier integrity. The anti-neuroinflammatory effect was mediated via the SCFA-associated FFAR3/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling pathway.
key_finding_ja: Faecalibacterium prausnitziiの投与は、短鎖脂肪酸/FFAR3/NF-κB/NLRP3経路を介して神経炎症を抑制し、糖尿病モデルマウスの不安・うつ様行動を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌やその代謝産物を活用したアプローチが、糖尿病に伴う情感障害の新たな管理戦略となる可能性が示唆されます。

title: Beyond stool: sampling context and inferential scope in gut mechanistic studies.
abstract: SUMMARYHuman gut microbiome research still relies heavily on fecal sampling because stool is noninvasive, scalable, repeatable, and essential for population-level and longitudinal studies. These strengths have made stool central to human microbiome science, but fecal output is not a neutral representation of every intestinal compartment. It reflects material that has persisted through digestion, transport, microbial turnover, host absorption, and distal colonic processing. This distinction becomes important when studies move from detecting microbial associations to explaining localized activity, host-interface interaction, inducible viral states, metabolic flux, or clinical consequences. This review proposes a framework for aligning sampling context with inferential scope across five evidence domains. These include distal output detection, regional luminal measurement, host-interface measurement, linked functional response, and patient-level consequence. The framework is not intended to rank specimen types or require every study to escalate toward invasive sampling. Instead, it clarifies which claims are supported by stool, luminal sampling, mucosal or host-proximal measurements, experimental models, and clinical metadata when used alone or in combination. Prophage induction and fecal short-chain fatty acid measurements are used as examples of a broader methodological issue. Detection in feces can be highly informative, but it does not by itself localize activity, establish mechanism, or demonstrate host consequence. As gut microbiome research increasingly seeks mechanistic explanations, sampling strategy should be treated as part of inference itself.
authors: Lewandowski R.
journal: Microbiology and molecular biology reviews : MMBR
screening_reason: The paper provides a methodological framework focused specifically on gut microbiome research, mucosal interface sampling, and microbial activity.
summary_ja: 本レビューでは、ヒト腸内細菌叢研究における糞便サンプリングの有用性と、そのデータから導き出せる生物学的推論の限界について論じている。著者らはサンプルの性質と推論範囲を整合させるため、遠位排出物検出や局所腔内測定など5つのエビデンス領域からなる統合的フレームワークを提案した。プロファージ誘導や短鎖脂肪酸の測定を例に挙げ、糞便中での検出結果のみでは腸管局所の機序や宿主への影響を直接証明できないことを強調している。
summary_en: This review addresses the conceptual gap between fecal sampling and localized mechanistic claims in human gut microbiome research. The authors introduce a framework across five evidence domains to guide the proper alignment of specimen types with their inferential boundaries. Using examples such as prophage induction and fecal short-chain fatty acids, the paper highlights that fecal measurements alone do not prove localized host-microbe interactions or biological mechanisms.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢研究において糞便データから推論できる範囲を明確化し、機序解明に資するための5つのエビデンス領域フレームワークが提案された。
why_it_matters_ja: 非侵襲的な糞便解析結果の過剰解釈を防ぎ、今後の腸内細菌研究における適切な実験計画やサンプリング戦略の策定に寄与する。

title: Exercise-driven microbiome changes regulate host immunity.
abstract: Exercise reshapes host physiology and immunity, yet the mechanisms linking physical activity to disease protection remain incompletely defined. Emerging evidence indicates that exercise remodels the gut microbiome, producing compositional and metabolic adaptations that can regulate immune function. In this Review, we discuss how exercise-responsive microbiota and microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, and the one-carbon metabolite formate, influence systemic inflammation, antitumor CD8 T-cell immunity, autoimmunity, and metabolic disease. Defining causal taxa, microbial metabolic pathways, and host-sensing mechanisms may enable microbiome-informed exercise prescriptions and targeted metabolite-, probiotic-, or postbiotic-based therapies.
authors: Phelps CM, Meisel M.
screening_reason: Focuses on exercise-induced alterations in the gut microbiome and microbial metabolites (SCFAs, formate) and their direct regulation of host immune function.
summary_ja: 運動は宿主の生理機能や免疫を変化させますが、疾患保護に至る明確なメカニズムは未解明な点が残されています。本総説では、物理的活動が腸内細菌叢および短鎖脂肪酸や二次胆汁酸などの代謝産物を再編し、免疫機能を調節する機序を解説しています。運動応答性の細菌群や代謝物が全身性炎症、抗腫瘍CD8 T細胞免疫、自己免疫、代謝性疾患に与える影響について議論されています。これらの知見は、腸内細菌叢に基づいた運動処方やポスカイオティクス療法の開発に寄与する可能性があります。
summary_en: This review outlines how exercise-induced modifications of the gut microbiome and microbial metabolites regulate host immune function. Key metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, and formate influence systemic inflammation, antitumor immunity, autoimmunity, and metabolic disease. Clarifying these microbial pathways may enable microbiome-informed exercise recommendations and metabolite-based therapeutics.
key_finding_ja: 運動による腸内細菌叢とその代謝産物の変化が、宿主の全身性炎症や抗腫瘍免疫などの免疫応答を調節することが示されている。
why_it_matters_ja: 運動による腸内微生物代謝の受容機構解明は、個別化運動処方や代謝物を用いた新たな免疫調節療法の開発に繋がる可能性があります。

title: Emerging roles of granzymes in neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation: mechanistic insights and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are increasingly recognized as disorders shaped not only by intrinsic neuronal vulnerability, but also by chronic neuroinflammation mediated by maladaptive neuroimmune signaling. Granzymes, a family of serine proteases classically studied for their cytotoxic roles in anti-viral and anti-tumor immunity, are emerging as important mediators of central nervous system (CNS) pathology. In addition to their canonical intracellular functions, granzymes can act extracellularly to cleave the extracellular matrix (ECM), activate cell-surface receptors, disrupt epithelial barrier function, amplify inflammatory cascades, and alter glial and neuronal responses to injury. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge on the roles of Granzyme A (GzmA), Granzyme B (GzmB), Granzyme H (GzmH), and Granzyme K (GzmK) in neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation across diverse CNS disease and injury contexts, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), multiple sclerosis (MS), stroke, spinal cord injury (SCI), and age-related macular degeneration (AMD). GzmB is the most extensively characterized, with evidence supporting both intracellular neurotoxicity and extracellular pathogenic functions mediated through protease-activated receptor signaling, ECM cleavage, outer blood-retina barrier disruption, angiogenesis, fibrosis, and chronic inflammation. GzmA is implicated in tau proteolysis and structural destabilization of neurons and astrocytes, while GzmK has emerged as a context-dependent regulator of neuroinflammation through PAR-1 activation, microglial modulation, and complement cascade activation. GzmH remains the least understood but may contribute to nerve injury through mechanisms that are only beginning to be defined. We also discuss endogenous and pharmacological granzyme inhibition, highlighting the therapeutic promise of selective extracellular granzyme targeting, particularly for GzmB, while emphasizing the current lack of selective inhibitors for GzmA, GzmK, and GzmH. Collectively, these findings position granzymes as underappreciated neuroimmune effectors and potential therapeutic targets in neurodegenerative diseases and CNS injury.
authors: Yoo HS, Yu P, Zhou C, Hosseini A, Granville DJ, Matsubara JA.
screening_reason: Investigates the mechanisms of granzymes as key neuroimmune effectors mediating neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in the central nervous system.
summary_ja: グランザイムは主に細胞傷害性セリンプロテアーゼとして知られていますが、中枢神経系（CNS）の病態生理における役割に注目が集まっています。本総説では、Granzyme A、B、H、Kの神経変性疾患や神経炎症における役割とメカニズムを整理しています。特にGzmBは細胞外基質の分解や炎症カスケードの増幅に関与することが示されています。これらの知見から、選択的なグランザイム阻害がCNS疾患に対する新たな治療アプローチとして期待されています。
summary_en: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the roles of Granzymes A, B, H, and K in neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation across diverse central nervous system disorders. Granzymes exert both intracellular cytotoxic effects and extracellular pathogenic functions, including extracellular matrix cleavage, receptor activation, and inflammatory cascade amplification. The authors discuss the therapeutic potential of targeting extracellular granzymes, particularly GzmB.
key_finding_ja: グランザイムファミリーは、細胞外基質分解や受容体信号伝達などを介して中枢神経系の炎症および神経変性を増幅する効果因子である。
why_it_matters_ja: グランザイムを選択的に標的とする阻害戦略が、神経変性疾患や中枢神経損傷に対する新たな治療法として期待されます。

title: Blocking the m 6 Am methyltransferase PCIF1 in macrophages attenuates colitis progression by preventing neuronal damage.
abstract: Macrophage-enteric neuron dialog is crucial for intestinal homeostasis, but its specific role and underlying mechanism in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) pathogenesis remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that colonic macrophage-mediated extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling orchestrates enteric neuronal maturation and dictates colitis progression. The depletion of Pcif1, recognized as a unique methyltransferase for m 6 Am mRNA methylation, in macrophages attenuates colitis and protects enteric neurons from inflammation-driven degeneration. Specifically, Pcif1-deficient macrophages increase ECM accumulation, promoting their own extravasation into enteric neuronal plexuses and the maturation of enteric neurons, thereby curbing inflammation-driven neuronal injury and colitis progression. Mechanistically, Pcif1-mediated m 6 Am modification inhibits the translation of Znf219 mRNA and represses the Znf219-Egr1 axis, a master transcriptional module that governs ECM remodeling. Finally, pharmacological blockade of PCIF1 promotes macrophage-mediated ECM deposition and suppresses colitis and neuronal loss. Our findings reveal a novel mechanism whereby ECM remodeling in macrophages drives enteric neuronal maturation and illuminate the m 6 Am machinery as a promising therapeutic target for preventing neuronal loss in IBD patients.
authors: Ding C, Zhao J, Zhao T, Xiao Y, Li K, Liu X, Ge X, Qin D, Huang Z, Zhang Y, Liu H, Diao Z, Ye Y, Flavell RA, Luo C, Chen S, Yi C, Wang Z, Li HB.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates the crosstalk between colonic macrophages and enteric neurons during colitis and enteric neuronal degeneration.
summary_ja: 本研究は、潰瘍性大腸炎などの炎症性腸疾患の病態におけるマクロファージと腸管神経の相互作用メカニズムを解明した。マクロファージにおけるmRNAのm6Am修飾酵素PCIF1を欠損させると、細胞外基質（ECM）の蓄積が促進され、マクロファージの腸管神経叢への浸潤と腸管神経の成熟が誘導された。このプロセスにより、炎症に伴う神経変性と大腸炎の進行が抑制されることが明らかになった。機序としては、PCIF1によるm6Am修飾の抑制がZnf219-Egr1転写軸を活性化し、ECMリモデリングを駆動することが示された。
summary_en: This study demonstrates that colonic macrophage-mediated extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling regulates enteric neuronal maturation and colitis progression. Depleting or pharmacologically inhibiting the m6Am methyltransferase PCIF1 in macrophages promoted ECM accumulation, facilitating macrophage extravasation into enteric neuronal plexuses and protecting enteric neurons from inflammatory damage. This pathway operates via the Znf219-Egr1 transcriptional module, identifying PCIF1 as a promising target to preserve enteric neurons in inflammatory bowel disease.
key_finding_ja: マクロファージのPCIF1を阻害すると、細胞外基質のリモデリングを介して腸管神経の成熟と保護が促進され、大腸炎の進行が抑制された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸管における免疫細胞と神経系の相互作用メカニズムが明示されたことで、炎症性腸疾患に伴う神経脱落を防止する新しい治療戦略の確立が期待される。

title: Artificial Intelligence in Post-translational Modification Site Prediction: Progress and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are pivotal in modulating protein function and cellular processes. However, experimental identification of PTM sites remains costly and labor-intensive. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled accurate and scalable in silico PTM site prediction from large-scale proteomic data. In this review, we provide a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of AI-driven PTM site prediction across more than ten PTM classes, covering single-PTM site prediction, multiple-PTM site prediction, inter-site crosstalk prediction, and functional prediction of modification sites. We systematically analyze and compare key AI frameworks, from conventional machine learning to deep learning, and summarize representative tools. We also identify key challenges and propose future directions for improvement. To facilitate application and ongoing progress, we provide practical guidelines for method selection and have established a dedicated website, which serves as a community benchmarking resource for the development of PTM site prediction tools. This website will be regularly updated with emerging prediction tools. By integrating comprehensive literature analysis with a dynamic online resource, we aim to provide a reliable foundation for understanding current capabilities and guiding the future development of PTM site prediction tools, thereby promoting the integration of AI into practical biomedical research applications.
authors: Ran J, Zhang X, Wang Y, Chen S, Deng J, Kosar M, Yang B, Wang H, Deng Y, Li T, Liu Y, Wang L, Guo Y, Zhang X, Huang H, Zhou J, Zheng J, Xu Z, Tang Y, Liu J.
screening_reason: The review focuses centrally on artificial intelligence frameworks for post-translational modification (PTM) site prediction.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、人工知能（AI）を活用したタンパク質の翻訳後修飾（PTM）部位予測技術の進展と展望を包括的に解説している。10種類以上のPTMクラスを対象に、従来の機械学習からディープラーニングに至るAIモデルや代表的ツールを比較分析した。また、適切なモデル選択のためのガイドラインを提示し、予測ツールの評価を行うコミュニティ用ウェブサイトを開設したことを報告している。
summary_en: This review summarizes recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods for predicting protein post-translational modification (PTM) sites across more than ten PTM classes. The authors systematically compare machine learning and deep learning tools for single- and multi-site modifications as well as inter-site crosstalk. Furthermore, practical guidelines and a community benchmark website are introduced to facilitate method selection and software development.
key_finding_ja: AIを用いたタンパク質翻訳後修飾（PTM）部位予測手法の比較分析が行われ、研究支援および精度検証のためのオンラインリソースが構築された。
why_it_matters_ja: 実験的特定に多大なコストがかかる修飾部位のインシリコ予測精度向上を支援し、大規模プロテオミクス解析や創薬研究の効率化に資することが期待される。

title: The hypusine circuit: eIF5A at the crossroads of polyamine metabolism, malignant progression, and therapeutic vulnerability.
abstract: Hypusination of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 5 A (eIF5A) is a highly conserved post-translational modification. This process uniquely depends on spermidine and is catalyzed sequentially by deoxyhypusine synthase (DHPS) and deoxyhypusine hydroxylase (DOHH). Recent studies have established eIF5A hypusination as a key translational regulatory mechanism linking polyamine metabolism to tumor progression. By relieving ribosomal stalling in selected difficult-to-translate targets, hypusinated eIF5A directly controls defined translational outputs. Through these direct mechanisms, as well as broader downstream signaling and phenotypic effects whose immediate translational targets remain incompletely resolved, the hypusination pathway has been linked to tumor cell proliferation, invasion and metastasis, angiogenesis, therapeutic resistance, and adaptive stress responses. This review critically distinguishes sequence-resolved translational mechanisms from target-level regulatory associations and indirect phenotypic consequences through which eIF5A hypusination is linked to these cancer hallmarks and further examines pharmacological and genetic strategies targeting the polyamine-eIF5A axis, including inhibitors of polyamine metabolism, DHPS, and DOHH. It also discusses the potential translational significance of these strategies in cancer therapy. Overall, eIF5A hypusination may act as a central effector that converts metabolic inputs into oncogenic protein outputs and represents a promising therapeutic target across diverse tumor types.
authors: Wen Z, Zeng Z, Xiong W, Fan C.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Reviews on cancer
screening_reason: The review focuses specifically on eIF5A hypusination, a unique covalent protein post-translational modification, and its translational regulatory mechanisms in cancer.
summary_ja: 本レビュー論文は、真核生物翻訳開始因子5A（eIF5A）のヒプシン化と呼ばれるタンパク質翻訳後修飾に焦点を当てている。ヒプシン化はスペルミジンに依存し、DHPSおよびDOHH酵素によって触媒され、特定の翻訳障害を緩和することで腫瘍の進展や治療抵抗性を制御する。本稿では、リボソーム停滞の解消といった直接的メカニズムと、増殖や浸潤などの表現型への間接的影響を区別して整理している。さらに、ポリアミン-eIF5A軸を標的とした薬理学的・遺伝学的治療戦略の可能性について概説している。
summary_en: This review discusses the hypusination of eIF5A, a unique post-translational modification dependent on spermidine and catalyzed by DHPS and DOHH. It outlines how hypusinated eIF5A regulates tumor progression, cell proliferation, invasion, and therapeutic resistance by relieving ribosomal stalling. The authors also highlight translational opportunities for targeting the polyamine-eIF5A pathway in cancer therapy.
key_finding_ja: eIF5Aのヒプシン化修飾がポリアミン代謝と腫瘍の悪性進展を結ぶ中核的な翻訳調節機構であり、がん治療の標的となり得ることがまとめられた。
why_it_matters_ja: ポリアミン代謝と翻訳修飾を標的とした新たな抗がん治療戦略の開発に貢献する可能性がある。

title: Synthetic microbial communities: emerging live biotherapeutics for targeted gut microbiome modulation.
abstract: Gut microbiome dysbiosis causes various intestinal diseases. However, an undefined composition and potential biosafety risks limit the applicability of traditional fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs), which are compositionally defined and rationally designed emerging live biotherapeutics, offer a novel alternative to FMT. This review establishes strict boundaries between SynComs and traditional donor-derived preparations, comparatively evaluating "top-down" and "bottom-up" construction strategies. We explored the mechanisms underlying the SynComs-mediated synergistic restoration of intestinal homeostasis via direct targeted antagonism and modulation of the host immune network. Moreover, we systematically evaluated the current research landscape of SynComs in Clostridioides difficile infection, inflammatory bowel disease, and colorectal cancer. This review examines fundamental challenges, including host colonization resistance, chemistry, manufacturing, and control barriers, biosafety risks, and microbiokinetic regulatory frameworks, thereby addressing the translational gap. Our analysis of current literature provides a theoretical basis for the clinical translation of SynComs as emerging live biotherapeutics.
authors: Zhang R, Li H, Wang C, Yang G.
screening_reason: Focuses directly on synthetic microbial communities for targeted gut microbiome modulation and intestinal homeostasis.
summary_ja: 本レビューでは、従来の糞便微生物移植（FMT）に代わる定義された組成の生体内製剤として、人工微生物叢（SynComs）の構築と応用に関する現状が解説されている。「トップダウン」および「ボトムアップ」の構築手法を比較するとともに、病原体への直接的対抗や宿主免疫ネットワークの調律を介した腸内恒常性維持機構が論じられている。さらに、Clostridioides difficile感染症、炎症性腸疾患、大腸癌におけるSynComsの研究動向を総括している。定着抵抗性や製造品質管理（CMC）、生物学的安全性、規制枠組みなどの定着・実用化に向けた課題についても網羅的に考察されている。
summary_en: This review evaluates synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) as rationally designed live biotherapeutic alternatives to traditional fecal microbiota transplantation. It compares top-down and bottom-up assembly strategies and details mechanisms of action, including direct antagonism and host immune network modulation. The article summarizes current applications in Clostridioides difficile infection, inflammatory bowel disease, and colorectal cancer while addressing key translational challenges such as colonization resistance, biosafety, and regulatory compliance.
key_finding_ja: 人工微生物叢（SynComs）は、精密に設計された生体内製剤として、直接的拮抗作用や免疫調節を介して腸内恒常性を標的復元する新しい治療法となり得る。
why_it_matters_ja: 従来型FMTの安全面や未定義性の課題を克服するSynComsの臨床応用が進むことで、各種腸疾患に対する標準化された微生物療法の実現が期待される。

title: Melatonin Ameliorates Neuropathic Pain in Mice by Regulating Pyroptosis Through Gut Microbiota-Mediated Linoleic Acid.
abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) presents a significant challenge for patients with chronic diseases, characterized by spontaneous pain and hyperalgesia, with recent studies highlighting the involvement of the gut microbiota in its pathogenesis. Increasing evidence suggests that melatonin mitigates systemic inflammation and remodels gut microbiota. The present study further explored the mechanism by which oral melatonin ameliorates pain-related behavior following peripheral nerve injury. In this study, mice with chronic constriction injury (CCI) were orally administered melatonin (100 mg/kg) for 14 days. Pain behaviors were evaluated using mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia tests. Gut microbiota profiles were assessed via 16S rRNA sequencing, and microbiota-dependent effects were verified through antibiotic treatment (ABX) and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). Linoleic acid (LA) levels in serum and spinal cord were measured using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), and protein expression of NLRP3, caspase-1, and GSDMD in spinal cord tissue was examined by immunoblotting. Melatonin treatment significantly increased the mechanical pain threshold and prolonged thermal withdrawal latency in CCI mice. It also remodeled the dysbiotic gut microbiota, and these protective effects were abolished by antibiotic treatment but restored by FMT. Protein analysis revealed upregulation of NLRP3 and GSDMD in CCI mice, both of which were suppressed following melatonin administration. Moreover, melatonin-induced microbiota modulation elevated LA levels in serum and spinal cord. Supplementation with LA alone alleviated NP and inhibited NLRP3, caspase-1, and GSDMD activation. These findings suggest that oral melatonin treatment effectively ameliorates NP in CCI mice associated with the neuroinflammation and microbiota-metabolites-brain axis.
authors: Wang Y, Yuan B, Li Y, Sun Y, Xie Y, Cheng H, Zhang Y, Wu Q, Tang J.
screening_reason: Examines how gut microbiota and microbial metabolites (linoleic acid) mediate melatonin's attenuation of neuroinflammation and neuropathic pain.
summary_ja: 坐骨神経慢性圧迫損傷（CCI）マウスモデルを用いて、メラトニン経口投与が神経障害性疼痛を緩和するメカニズムが調査された。メラトニン投与は、腸内細菌叢の異常を是正し、血清および脊髄におけるリノール酸（LA）レベルを上昇させるとともに、痛覚過敏行動を抑制した。腸内細菌叢の除去（ABX）によりこの効果は消失し、糞便微生物移植（FMT）によって回復した。さらに、メラトニンおよびLA直接投与は、脊髄におけるNLRP3、caspase-1、GSDMDを介したパイロトーシス経路の活性化を抑制することが示された。
summary_en: Oral administration of melatonin alleviated neuropathic pain behaviors in a mouse model of chronic constriction injury. Melatonin restored gut microbiota composition and increased linoleic acid levels in serum and spinal cord, suppressing NLRP3- and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis in the spinal cord. Antibiotic depletion abolished these beneficial effects, whereas fecal microbiota transplantation restored them.
key_finding_ja: メラトニンは腸内細菌叢由来のリノール酸増加を介して脊髄におけるパイロトーシスを抑制し、神経障害性疼痛を緩和する。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢-代謝物-脳軸を通じた神経炎症制御機構の解明は、慢性神経障害性疼痛に対する新たな治療法開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Serum-Cecal Metabolome Integration Predicts Gut Microbial Communities and Reveals Pathway-Level Host-Microbe Crosstalk Under Disease-Induced Dysbiosis.
abstract: The gut microbiome shapes systemic physiology through metabolites that enter circulation, yet most computational approaches focus on predicting metabolite profiles from microbial features rather than inferring microbial composition from host metabolomes. Here, we investigate whether host-derived metabolomic profiles can be leveraged to predict gut microbial community structure and to determine how disease-associated dysbiosis reshapes metabolite-microbe interactions and gut-to-systemic metabolic communication. We developed an integrative multi-omics framework combining serum and cecal metabolomics with 16S rRNA-based microbiome profiling. Supervised learning models demonstrated that cecal metabolites carry predictive signals for microbial abundances across conditions. Regularized canonical correlation analysis (rCCA) revealed cross-compartment metabolite-microbe networks. These analyses showed both conserved and condition-specific interaction patterns, indicating substantial network reorganization under disease-associated dysbiosis. Pathway-level integration further identified metabolic pathways linking the gut microbiome, the cecal environment, and the systemic circulation, representing coordinated gut-to-systemic communication axes. Together, our results establish a multi-omics strategy for predictive inference of gut microbial composition from host metabolomes and provide a framework for identifying pathway-level mechanisms underlying host-microbe metabolic crosstalk.
authors: Baidya AK, Aich P.
journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
screening_reason: Focuses directly on host metabolome integration to predict gut microbial composition and analyze gut-host metabolic crosstalk.
summary_ja: 宿主の代謝物プロファイルから腸内細菌叢の組成を逆予測し、病態時の網羅的クロストークを解析するためのマルチオミクス統合フレームワークが開発された。血清および盲腸の代謝物データと16S rRNA細菌叢解析を組み合わせることで、盲腸代謝物が細菌存在量の予測シグナルを保持していることが確認された。正則化正準相関分析（rCCA）により、健常時と病態時の双方向代謝物-細菌ネットワークが構築され、菌群異常（ディスバイオーシス）下での著しい構造再編が示された。さらに、腸管から全身循環へと至るパスウェイレベルの代謝伝達軸が特定された。
summary_en: An integrative multi-omics framework combining serum and cecal metabolomics with 16S rRNA sequencing was developed to infer gut microbial community composition from host metabolomic profiles. Cecal metabolites effectively predicted microbial abundances, and regularized canonical correlation analysis identified condition-specific microbial-metabolite networks. The analysis further highlighted pathway-level metabolic axes connecting the gut environment to systemic circulation under disease-induced dysbiosis.
key_finding_ja: 宿主の盲腸および血清代謝物プロファイルを用いることで、腸内細菌叢の組成を予測可能であり、病態によるディスバイオーシス下での網羅的クロストークの再編成が明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 宿主代謝データに基づく細菌叢推測および全身性代謝クロストーク解析の手法は、微生物叢が及ぼす全身性疾患メカニズムの特定に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Seasonal Dynamics of Community and Function of Gut Microbiome in Taihangshan Macaque (Macaca mulatta tcheliensis): Inferred From Metagenomic Data.
abstract: The gut microbiome is a key regulator of host nutritional intake, growth, and health, playing an essential role in mediating host adaptation to environmental changes. The northernmost population of rhesus macaque, Taihangshan macaque (Macaca mulatta tcheliensis), faces severe survival challenges, such as food shortages and harsh temperatures during winter and early spring. Previous studies have shown that they cope with seasonal changes through behavioral adaptations, such as adjusting food resources and flexibly regulating macronutrient intake. However, the role of the gut microbiome in supporting the seasonal adaptation of Taihangshan macaques remains unclear. Herein, we investigated seasonal variations in gut microbiome alpha diversity, composition, and functions from fecal samples of Taihangshan macaques using metagenomic analysis. The results showed that: (1) totally 435 non-redundant metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs) were generated; (2) alpha diversity was significantly higher in spring and winter than in summer and autumn; and (3) in winter, pathways of fatty acid biosynthesis and essential amino acid (EAA) biosynthesis, as well as CAZymes (GH3 and GH5) involved in cellulose and hemicellulose degradation, were significantly enriched. In contrast, pathways related to carbohydrate, energy, and glycan biosynthesis and metabolism, along with CAZymes (GT8 and GH23) potentially facilitating fat synthesis and storage, were enriched in summer. These functional adjustments likely help the host cope with seasonal variations in food availability and environmental conditions. Overall, this study provides new insights into how the gut microbiome responds to seasonal changes in diet and environmental factors in mammals inhabiting temperate forests.
authors: Zhou Y, Shao Q, Liu C, Tian J, Guan X, Zhang X, Lu J.
screening_reason: Metagenomic study directly characterizing seasonal community and functional dynamics of the gut microbiome in macaque monkeys.
summary_ja: 寒冷地かつ食料資源の制限を受ける太行山アカゲザル（Macaca mulatta tcheliensis）の糞便サンプルを用いたメタゲノム解析により、腸内細菌叢の季節的変化と機能的順応が調べられた。解析の結果、腸内細菌叢のα多様性は夏や秋と比較して春および冬に有意に高かった。冬期には脂肪酸および必須アミノ酸の合成経路や、セルロース・ヘミセルロース分解に関与するCAZyme（GH3、GH5）が有意に濃縮されていた。一方、夏期には炭水化物代謝経路や脂質合成・蓄積を促進するCAZyme（GT8、GH23）が豊富であった。
summary_en: Metagenomic profiling of fecal samples from Taihangshan macaques revealed seasonal shifts in gut microbiome composition and functional potential. Microbial alpha diversity was significantly higher during spring and winter compared to summer and autumn. Functional pathways for fatty acid and essential amino acid biosynthesis were enriched in winter, whereas carbohydrate and glycan metabolic pathways predominated in summer.
key_finding_ja: 太行山アカゲザルの腸内細菌叢は、冬期の繊維分解・必須栄養素合成と夏期のエネルギー蓄積代謝という季節的変化に応じた機能的シフトを示す。
why_it_matters_ja: 霊長類が環境や食餌の季節変動に適応するための腸内細菌叢の役割を解明することは、宿主と微生物の共生適応メカニズムの理解に貢献する。

title: Endocannabinoids and related lipids in host metabolism-gut microbiome signalling.
abstract: Over the past two decades, it has become clear that the two endocannabinoids, anandamide and 2-arachidonoyl-glycerol, are only the tip of an iceberg of a larger signalling system composed of hundreds of chemically similar fatty acid derivatives, including 2-monoacylglycerols, N-acylethanolamines and other N-acylamines. Unlike the endocannabinoids, these lipids only seldom bind the two cannabinoid receptors, of which CB1 is now recognized as a major player in both the central and peripheral control of energy metabolism. They modulate instead the activity of other G-protein-coupled receptors, as well as of ligand-activated ion channels and nuclear receptors, which also regulate energy intake, accumulation and expenditure. Bacteria inhabiting the gut as part of the intestinal microbiome also produce endocannabinoid-like molecules capable of activating host receptors in vitro. These discoveries led to current research into potential bi-directional communication between this 'extended endocannabinoid system', or endocannabinoidome, and the gut microbiome. Ongoing studies are investigating how this axis might control energy metabolism, particularly in response to diet.
authors: Silvestri C, Di Marzo V.
screening_reason: The article focuses directly on bidirectional signaling between the gut microbiome and host metabolism via endocannabinoids and related lipid signaling.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、エンドカンナビノイドおよびその類似脂質群（エンドカンナビノイドム）と腸内細菌叢との相互作用について論じている。これらの脂質メディエーターはカンナビノイド受容体やその他のGPCR、イオンチャネルなどを介してエネルギー代謝や摂食を調節する。腸内細菌もエンドカンナビノイド様分子を産生して宿主受容体を活性化することが分かっており、両者の双方向通信が注目されている。本稿では、食事応答やエネルギー代謝制御におけるこの拡大エンドカンナビノイドシステムと腸内細菌叢軸の役割を解説している。
summary_en: This review explores the bidirectional communication between the extended endocannabinoid system (endocannabinoidome) and the gut microbiome in regulating energy metabolism. In addition to classical endocannabinoids, numerous related lipid derivatives modulate host energy homeostasis through diverse receptors, while gut bacteria synthesize structurally similar lipids that activate these host pathways. The article highlights current insights into how this host-microbiome lipid signaling axis influences metabolic outcomes in response to diet.
key_finding_ja: 宿主のエンドカンナビノイドムと腸内細菌叢が産生する類似脂質との双方向シグナル伝達が、エネルギー代謝の制御に関与している。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事や腸内細菌叢に由来する脂質シグナルの解明が進むことで、代謝性疾患に対する新たな栄養的・薬学的介入アプローチの発見につながる可能性がある。

title: TAB2 Causes Neuronal Damage by Aggravating Microglia-Mediated Neuroinflammation in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Neuroinflammation plays a key role in exacerbating dopaminergic neuron loss in Parkinson's disease (PD). We identified TAB2 as an early-stage biomarker, which was elevated in PD patients' microglia. However, the role of TAB2 in the pathogenesis of PD remains unknown. In this study, we found that Tab2 knockdown inhibited the activation of microglia and protected neurons in PD models. STAT3, as a transcription factor for TAB2, regulated TAB2 expression. Mechanistically, TAB2 interacted with α-synuclein and facilitated the recognition of K63-linked ubiquitin chains, leading to the formation of the TAK1-TABs complex and activation of TAK1, which was ultimately followed by activation of the nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling pathway. Furthermore, microglia-specific knockdown of Tab2 significantly inhibited microglia activation, protected dopaminergic neurons, improved motor function, and attenuated anxiety-like behaviors in PD mouse model. We further showed that the FDA-approved drug, lumacaftor, suppressed microglial TAB2 expression and had potent anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects in PD models. Taken together, our study reveals that the STAT3-TAB2-NF-κB-IL-1β positive feedback axis in microglia is a crucial checkpoint that exacerbates neuroinflammation in PD. Therefore, these findings identify a pivotal role of TAB2 in regulating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation, suggesting that targeting TAB2 may be a possible therapeutic strategy for PD.
authors: Zhao Y, Huang Z, Gao J, Li A, Wang H, Chen Y, Zhu G, Zhang X, Jiang Y, Zhang M, Meng F, Zhang J, Du T.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates microglial-mediated neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease and defines the STAT3-TAB2-NF-kB signaling pathway.
summary_ja: パーキンソン病（PD）におけるドパミン作動性神経脱落の増悪因子として、ミクログリアを介した神経炎症が知られている。本研究では、PD患者のミクログリアで増加しているTAB2が、αシヌクレインとの相互作用やK63型ポリウビキチン鎖の認識促進を通じてTAK1-NF-κB経路を活性化することを示した。マウスPDモデルにおいてミクログリア特異的にTab2をノックダウンすると、ミクログリア活性化の抑制、ドパミン作動性神経の保護、運動機能障害および不安様行動の改善が認められた。さらに、既存薬のルマカフトルがTAB2発現を抑え、神経保護効果を発揮することが見出された。
summary_en: This study reveals that microglial TAB2 plays a critical role in Parkinson's disease (PD) pathogenesis by exacerbating neuroinflammation via the STAT3-TAB2-NF-κB-IL-1β signaling axis. Knockdown of Tab2 in microglia inhibited microglial activation, protected dopaminergic neurons, and improved motor and emotional deficits in PD mouse models. Additionally, the FDA-approved drug lumacaftor suppressed TAB2 expression and conferred neuroprotective effects.
key_finding_ja: TAB2がミクログリアにおけるNF-κB炎症経路を増幅してパーキンソン病の神経炎症と神経脱落を引き起こす重要因子であることを解明した。
why_it_matters_ja: TAB2を標的とした治療アプローチやルマカフトルのドラッグリポジショニングが、パーキンソン病の新しい神経保護療法に繋がる可能性がある。

title: Pyroptosis in Alzheimer's disease: Mechanisms and neuroinflammatory networks.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder pathologically characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau protein hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and sustained neuroinflammation. In recent years, pyroptosis, a gasdermin-mediated form of inflammatory programmed cell death, has been recognized as a potential mechanism linking innate immune activation to neurodegenerative injury. This review summarizes the major molecular pathways of pyroptosis, including the canonical inflammasome-caspase-1-GSDMD pathway, the noncanonical caspase-4/5/11-GSDMD pathway, and alternative pathways involving caspase-3/GSDME and caspase-8, with a focus on their roles in the initiation, amplification, and propagation of neuroinflammation in AD. Current evidence suggests that AD-related stimuli, including Aβ aggregation, tau pathology, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and lysosomal damage, can induce inflammasome activation, gasdermin cleavage, and inflammatory mediator release, thereby sustaining chronic neuroinflammation. Concurrently, microglia, neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes may exhibit varying degrees of pyroptosis-related responses, contributing to impaired Aβ clearance, neuronal injury, glial dysfunction, and myelin pathology, respectively. This review further summarizes potential therapeutic strategies targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome, caspases, gasdermins, natural bioactive compounds, and the gut-brain axis. Overall, pyroptosis provides a novel framework for understanding the interplay between neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in AD; however, its cell-type-specific roles, stage-dependent effects, and translational potential remain to be fully elucidated.
authors: Wu X, Ye Q, Zi M, Jiang H, Meng S, Zheng J, Zeng S, Ma C, Hu X, Zhao B, Li H.
screening_reason: Review centered on pyroptosis pathways, gasdermin activation, and neuroinflammatory networks in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: 本総説は、アルツハイマー病（AD）におけるパイロトーシスの分子メカニズムと神経炎症ネットワークの関与について整理しています。アミロイドβやタウの病理、ミトコンドリア障害、酸化ストレスなどのAD関連刺激がインフラマソームを活性化し、ガスカドミン切断や炎症性因子の放出を引き起こします。ミクログリアやニューロン、アストロサイト、オリゴデンドロサイトにおけるパイロトーシス関連反応が、Aβクリアランス障害や神経損傷、脱髄病理に寄与することが説明されています。さらに、NLRP3インフラマソームやカスパアーゼ、ガスカドミン、腸脳軸を標的とした治療可能性についても触れられています。
summary_en: This review summarizes the molecular pathways of pyroptosis and its involvement in neuroinflammatory networks in Alzheimer's disease. Pathological stimuli such as amyloid-beta, tau pathology, and oxidative stress induce inflammasome activation and gasdermin cleavage across various CNS cell types. The article also outlines potential therapeutic targets, including the NLRP3 inflammasome, caspases, gasdermins, and gut-brain axis pathways.
key_finding_ja: パイロトーシスはADにおける各種中枢神経細胞の障害や持続的な神経炎症の増幅に関与しており、病態進行を結ぶ新たなフレームワークを提供する。
why_it_matters_ja: ADにおける細胞種特異的かつ病期依存的なパイロトーシス制御の理解が、新たな治療アプローチの開発につながる可能性がある。

title: PARP inhibition attenuates neuroinflammation and demyelination in a rat model of multiple sclerosis: A longitudinal [ 11 C]PBR28 TSPO PET imaging study.
abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) plays important role in DNA repair, but is also involved in other cellular processes. PARP inhibition was suggested to suppress inflammatory signaling and has been proposed as potential treatment for neuroinflammatory disorders like multiple sclerosis. Yet, its effects on lesion-associated neuroinflammation in vivo remain insufficiently understood. We therefore evaluated whether the PARP inhibitor PJ34 can attenuate neuroinflammation and demyelination, and whether treatment response can be monitored longitudinally, using positron emission tomography (PET) with [ 11 C]PBR28, a tracer for glial activation. In vitro, PJ34 was found to reduce [ 11 C]PBR28 uptake and ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (IBA1) immunoreactivity in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. In vivo, focal demyelination was induced in male Sprague-Dawley rats by unilateral lysolecithin injection into the corpus callosum and striatum, followed by PJ34 or vehicle treatment and serial [ 11 C]PBR28 PET imaging on days 3 and 7. PET revealed significantly lower tracer uptake in lesions of PJ34-treated animals compared to vehicle controls on day 3 (SUV mean 1.21 vs. 1.75; p 11 C]PBR28 PET imaging as a sensitive noninvasive biomarker of treatment response.
authors: Li G, Antunes IF, Ming Z, Wu C, Cornelissen B, de Vries EF.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
screening_reason: Evaluates PARP inhibition to attenuate neuroinflammation and demyelination in a multiple sclerosis animal model using longitudinal PET imaging.
summary_ja: 本研究は、多発性硬化症のラットモデルにおいてPARP阻害剤PJ34が神経炎症と脱髄を抑制するかをPETイメージングを用いて評価しました。In vitroにおいてPJ34はLPS刺激マクロファージの[11C]PBR28集積およびIBA1発現を低減させました。リゾレシチン誘発脱髄ラットモデルでは、PJ34投与により3日目のPET画像で病変部のトレーサー集積が有意に低下し、7日目にはIBA1陽性細胞の減少および脱髄の軽減が確認されました。
summary_en: This study evaluated whether the PARP inhibitor PJ34 attenuates neuroinflammation and demyelination in a rat model of multiple sclerosis using [11C]PBR28 PET imaging. In vitro, PJ34 reduced tracer uptake and IBA1 immunoreactivity in LPS-stimulated macrophages. In vivo, PJ34-treated rats exhibited significantly lower lesion tracer uptake on day 3, along with reduced microglial/macrophage activation and attenuated demyelination on day 7.
key_finding_ja: PARP阻害剤PJ34の投与により、ラット脱髄モデルにおけるミクログリア/マクロファージの活性化、病変部の[11C]PBR28集積、および脱髄が有意に抑制された。
why_it_matters_ja: PARP阻害が多発性硬化症の病変関連神経炎症を抑制する治療標的となり得るほか、[11C]PBR28 PETが治療反応の非侵襲的モニタリングに有用である可能性を示している。

title: Innate immunity-mediated inflammation and immunopathogenesis in HSV-1-infected encephalitis.
abstract: HSV-1 encephalitis (HSE) remains a devastating viral infection of the central nervous system despite effective antiviral therapy. Increasing evidence indicates that disease outcome is not determined by viral replication alone but by how innate immunity is calibrated within the brain. Studies of host susceptibility in childhood HSE have identified brain-intrinsic antiviral mechanisms, referring to central nervous system (CNS)-localized innate immune pathways that enable resident brain cells to sense and restrict HSV-1 infection, particularly TLR-dependent interferon responses, neuron-associated restriction factors, and other CNS-resident innate immune mechanisms. Host innate immune responses initially contribute to viral restriction, whereas excessive or unresolved activation can promote inflammatory amplification and long-term neurological injury. In parallel, HSV-1-mediated immune remodeling may weaken antiviral control and alter the subsequent inflammatory trajectory. Here, HSE is discussed as a dynamic immunopathological disorder in which protective innate immunity can transition into pathogenic neuroinflammation. Building upon these observations, we propose that host-directed therapeutic strategies should shift from uniform immune modulation toward stage-specific immune recalibration on the basis of viral control, antiviral competence, inflammatory persistence, and tissue repair.
authors: Yang S, Shen Y, Zheng C.
screening_reason: Focuses directly on central nervous system innate immunity, neuroinflammation, and immunopathogenesis during HSV-1 encephalitis.
summary_ja: 本論文は、単純ヘルペスウイルス1型（HSV-1）脳炎における自然免疫応答と病態形成のメカニズムに関する知見をまとめた総説です。中枢神経系における自然免疫経路は初期のウイルス制御に寄与する一方で、過剰または制御不能な活性化は炎症の増幅や長期的神経損傷を引き起こします。ウイルス複製だけでなく、脳内における自然免疫の調整状態が病勢を左右することが指摘されています。著者らは、一律の免疫修飾ではなく、感染や炎症の段階に応じた段階的な免疫再調整治療へのシフトを提唱しています。
summary_en: This review discusses the role of innate immunity and immunopathogenesis in HSV-1 encephalitis. While CNS-intrinsic innate immune responses initially restrict viral infection, excessive or unresolved activation can drive inflammatory amplification and neurological injury. The authors propose shifting host-directed therapeutic strategies toward stage-specific immune recalibration based on viral control and inflammatory persistence.
key_finding_ja: HSV-1脳炎において、脳固有の自然免疫は初期のウイルス抑制に不可欠であるものの、過剰な活性化は増幅された神経炎症と組織損傷を引き起こす。
why_it_matters_ja: HSV-1脳炎に対する治療戦略を単なる免疫抑制から病相に応じた段階的免疫調節へ転換するための概念的基盤となる可能性がある。

title: Human gut microbiome as a composite health biomarker.
abstract: Using a cohort of 893 adults who underwent medical check-ups with rich data collection across diet, lifestyle, clinical labs, cardiac stress testing, and microbiome profiling, we show that a gut microbial health index (MHI), originally defined using a large meta-analysis of various human disease cohorts, is also substantially associated with lifestyle and diet. This association persists across the overall cohort, disease-free subsets, and individuals with common medical conditions such as hypertension and dyslipidemia. The gut MHI was positively correlated with factors such as variation in cardiac stress test fitness, fiber intake, and well-being, and negatively correlated with exposure to ultra-processed foods and markers of subclinical inflammation (WBC and CRP mostly within normal limits). Lipidomics profiling of a subcohort revealed that triglycerides correlate positively with ultraprocessed foods, and negatively with unsaturated fats, olive oil, and nuts, linking diet, MHI, and lipid profile. Estimating the contribution of modifiable dietary and lifestyle factors to the MHI uncovers actionable ways to improve or worsen the personal MHI. Analyses of previously published intervention studies showed that the MHI responds quickly to dietary changes, within the predicted range. Our findings emphasize the potential of using microbiomes, and specifically the MHI, as a reporter of overall health.
authors: Braun T, Harounian O, Hadar R, Ziv A, Ben-Avraham Shulman S, Kalter-Leibovici O, Efroni G, Ziv R, Fenesh M, Abbas-Egbariya H, Abramovich I, Amit S, Keller N, Truman K, Segev S, Amir A, Haberman Y.
screening_reason: The research focuses on assessing the human gut microbiome and gut microbial health index in relation to dietary, metabolic, and clinical parameters.
summary_ja: 893名の成人コホートを対象に、腸内細菌叢健康指数（MHI）と生活習慣、食事、体力、炎症マーカーの関連が解析されました。その結果、MHIは食物繊維摂取量や体力と正の相関を示し、超加工食品の摂取や潜在的炎症マーカーと負の相関を示しました。さらに介入研究の解析から、MHIは食事の変更に対して迅速に反応することが確認されました。これらの結果は、腸内細菌叢が全身の健康状態を反映する複合的なバイオマーカーとして有効であることを示しています。
summary_en: In a cohort of 893 adults, the gut microbial health index (MHI) was significantly associated with diet, lifestyle, physical fitness, and markers of subclinical inflammation. Lipidomics and intervention analyses showed that MHI correlates with dietary habits and responds rapidly to dietary modifications. These findings highlight the potential of using the gut microbiome and MHI as a composite reporter of overall health.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢健康指数（MHI）は食事や運動、炎症状態と密接に関連し、食事介入に対して迅速に変化することが示されました。
why_it_matters_ja: MHIが全身の健康や生活習慣を反映する有用な指標として、個人の健康評価や食事指導に応用できる可能性があります。

title: EXPRESS: Spleen-mediated inflammation in ischemic stroke: mechanisms and targeted therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Emerging evidence from animal studies and clinical observations suggests that peripheral immune responses amplify neuroinflammation after acute ischemic stroke. This review briefly summarizes the interactions between peripheral immune responses and the ischemic brain, with a focus on the brain-spleen axis. Specifically, we dissect the mechanisms underlying spleen-mediated immune effects on the ischemic brain. We then critically summarize current spleen-targeted therapeutic strategies, ranging from physical and pharmacological interventions to stem cell-based approaches that reprogram splenic immune landscapes. Collectively, these insights aim to inform future immunomodulatory strategies targeting the brain-spleen axis.
authors: Wu S, Luo LH, Gao Y, Nan G.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
screening_reason: The review centrally addresses peripheral immune-brain interactions and spleen-mediated neuroinflammation following acute ischemic stroke.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、虚血性脳卒中急性期後における脳と脾臓の相互作用軸（脳-脾臓軸）に焦点を当て、末梢免疫応答が脳内神経炎症を増幅するメカニズムを概括している。特に、脾臓が媒介する免疫効果と脳虚血病態への関与について整理している。さらに、物理的・薬理的介入や幹細胞を用いた脾臓の免疫環境再プログラミングなど、脾臓を標的とした最新の治療戦略を批判的にまとめている。これらの知見は、脳虚血に対する新たな免疫調節療法の開発に寄与することを目的としている。
summary_en: This review outlines the communication along the brain-spleen axis following acute ischemic stroke, emphasizing how peripheral immune responses driven by the spleen amplify central neuroinflammation. The authors detail the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms of spleen-mediated post-stroke immune responses. Additionally, they evaluate emerging spleen-targeted therapeutic strategies, including physical, pharmacological, and stem cell-based interventions aimed at reprogramming the splenic immune landscape.
key_finding_ja: 虚血性脳卒中後において、脾臓を中心とする末梢免疫応答が脳の神経炎症を増幅させるメカニズムと、その治療標的としての可能性が提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳-脾臓軸を介した末梢免疫制御システムへの介入は、脳卒中後の神経炎症軽減および脳損傷抑制のための新たな治療概念を提供する可能性がある。

title: The gut microbiome and allograft outcomes: implications for heart transplantation.
abstract: Heart transplantation remains the gold standard therapy for patients with end-stage heart failure. However, post-transplant complications are considerable. Emerging evidence implicates the gut microbiome as a modifiable determinant of post-heart transplant outcomes through its influence on host immunity, metabolism, and inflammation.
